section: Science, Technology and Innovation Policy - 1958 Resolution, 1983, 2003, 2013 policies and the STIP draft
subsections: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Science and Technology Policy, 2003 — Indira Gandhi
accepted.x: The Scientific Policy Resolution of 1958 was associated with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru. The other policies were associated with Indira Gandhi, A.B. Vajpayee and Manmohan Singh respectively.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure policy–Prime Minister pair and eliminate swapped authorities.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: The Scientific Policy Resolution of 1958 was India's first comprehensive policy relating to which field?
accepted.x: The Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958 was India's first comprehensive science and technology policy.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the policy’s defining historical distinction.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: Which of the following was an important institutional emphasis of the Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958?
o: Replacement of public laboratories by private firms
Creation of national laboratories and institutions
accepted.x: The 1958 Resolution emphasised the development of national laboratories and scientific institutions.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional measure directly associated with the policy.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Technology Policy Statement, 1983:
1. It emphasised technological competence and self-reliance.
2. It encouraged the development, absorption and adaptation of technology.
3. It sought to reduce dependence on imports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements correctly describe the Technology Policy Statement, 1983, associated with technological competence, self-reliance, technology absorption and reduced import dependence.
accepted.tq: Test a policy through its complete cluster of objectives; all three statements are supported.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: The Technology Policy Statement, 1983 was introduced during the Prime Ministership of:
accepted.x: The Technology Policy Statement was issued in 1983 during the Prime Ministership of Indira Gandhi.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related policy–Prime Minister pairs.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes a major contribution of the Science and Technology Policy, 2003?
o: It brought science and technology together and stressed investment in research and development
It focused exclusively on reducing imports
It introduced innovation as the central theme for the first time
It established One Nation, One Subscription
accepted.x: The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 brought science and technology together and stressed investment in research and development. Innovation as the central theme and One Nation, One Subscription belong to later policy developments.
accepted.tq: Separate the core thrusts of successive policies instead of matching a later idea to an earlier policy.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a stated objective associated with the Science and Technology Policy, 2003?
o: Establishment of One Nation, One Subscription
accepted.x: Sustainable development, poverty alleviation and quality of life were objectives of the 2003 policy. One Nation, One Subscription is associated with the Draft STIP 2020 and was approved much later.
accepted.tq: Find the later policy proposal inserted into an earlier policy’s objective list.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s:
Consider the following objectives of the Science and Technology Policy, 2003:
1. Promotion of research, innovation and technology transfer.
2. Sustainable development and poverty alleviation.
3. Improvement in quality of life.
4. Optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources.
Which of the objectives given above were associated with the policy?
accepted.x: All four objectives were associated with the Science and Technology Policy, 2003, including the optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources.
accepted.tq: Check whether the apparently less prominent fourth objective is also included before choosing the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 was associated with which Prime Minister?
accepted.x: The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 was introduced during the Prime Ministership of A.B. Vajpayee.
accepted.tq: Use the year to distinguish the policy from the 1983 and 2013 policies.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: The theme of the STI Policy, 2013 was:
o: Science, Technology and Innovation for the People
accepted.x: The theme of the STI Policy, 2013 was “Science, Technology and Innovation for the People.”
accepted.tq: Use the exact official phrase and distinguish innovation-centred wording from older policy themes.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the distinctive feature of the STI Policy, 2013?
o: It limited scientific activity to government laboratories
It was India's first national science and technology policy
It added innovation as a central component and aimed to place India among the top five scientific powers by 2020
It removed innovation from the science and technology framework
accepted.x: The STI Policy, 2013 made innovation central and set the objective of placing India among the top five scientific powers by 2020.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining addition and the associated target year.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following policies in chronological order:
A. STI Policy
B. Scientific Policy Resolution
C. Science and Technology Policy
D. Technology Policy Statement
accepted.x: The correct sequence is Scientific Policy Resolution, 1958; Technology Policy Statement, 1983; Science and Technology Policy, 2003; and STI Policy, 2013.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest policies first, then place the 1983 and 2003 policies between them.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: Which of the following targets was associated with the STI Policy, 2013?
o: Raise India's share of global publications from 3.5 per cent to over 7 per cent
Reduce India's share of global publications below 2 per cent
Limit research publications to the top 10 journals
Replace public research with imported technology
accepted.x: The STI Policy, 2013 targeted an increase in India's share of global publications from 3.5 per cent to more than 7 per cent.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the stated percentage target from reversed or reduced figures.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the STI Policy, 2013?
o: Creation of new public–private partnership structures
Quadrupling papers in the top one per cent of journals
accepted.x: The STI Policy, 2013 promoted high-risk innovation rather than abolishing it. It also envisaged quadrupling papers in top one per cent journals, enhancing private R&D and creating new PPP structures.
accepted.tq: Reject the option that reverses the policy’s innovation-supporting approach.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: The period from 2010 to 2020 was declared India's:
accepted.x: The period 2010–2020 was declared India's “Decade of Innovation.”
accepted.tq: Recall the exact title associated with the specified decade.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: The Draft STIP 2020 was projected as India's:
o: Sixth national science and technology policy
Third national science and technology policy
Fifth national science and technology policy
Fourth national science and technology policy
accepted.x: The Draft STIP 2020 was projected as India's fifth national science and technology policy.
accepted.tq: Test the ordinal number directly while using adjacent ordinals as plausible distractors.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly represents the broad approach of the Draft STIP 2020?
o: Decentralised, bottom-up, self-reliant and open science-oriented governance
Centralised, top-down and closed research governance
accepted.x: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed a decentralised and bottom-up approach, with emphasis on self-reliance, open science and equity.
accepted.tq: Match the policy’s multiple thrusts and reject the reversed centralised or closed model.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: The vision of the Draft STIP 2020 included making India:
o: A regional scientific power only by 2050
Dependent on the top three foreign research systems
The sole scientific superpower within five years
One of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade
accepted.x: The Draft STIP 2020 envisioned India becoming one of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade and proposed a people-centric STI ecosystem.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise ranking and time horizon rather than accepting an exaggerated claim.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Which of the following is associated with the Open Science Framework proposed under the Draft STIP 2020?
accepted.x: One Nation, One Subscription was proposed to provide pan-India access to research journals under the Open Science Framework.
accepted.tq: Link the named programme to its policy framework and purpose.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Which of the following funding mechanisms was proposed in the Draft STIP 2020?
o: National Research Foundation with hybrid funding involving private capital and CSR
Only foreign grants with no domestic contribution
accepted.x: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed a National Research Foundation and hybrid funding involving private capital and corporate social responsibility contributions.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy’s mixed public–private funding design.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: The STI Development Bank proposed under the Draft STIP 2020 was intended to provide:
accepted.x: The STI Development Bank was proposed as a corpus-based funding mechanism for long-term strategic areas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the purpose of a specialised institution from ordinary banking functions.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: STI Observatory — monitoring and knowledge support for science, technology and innovation
Strategic Technology Board — journal subscription service
STI Policy Institute — agricultural price regulation
accepted.x: The STI Observatory was among the institutional proposals of the Draft STIP 2020. RIEF refers to Research and Innovation Excellence Frameworks, while the Strategic Technology Board was intended to link strategic departments.
accepted.tq: Use the institutional name and reject distractors that assign it a neighbouring policy function.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Research and Innovation Excellence Frameworks proposed under the Draft STIP 2020 are abbreviated as:
accepted.x: Research and Innovation Excellence Frameworks are abbreviated as RIEF.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely similar abbreviations by expanding the official phrase.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: The Strategic Technology Board proposed under the Draft STIP 2020 was intended primarily to:
accepted.x: The Strategic Technology Board was proposed to link strategic departments and coordinate work in strategic technology areas.
accepted.tq: Ask which institutional function logically follows from the body’s name and policy role.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Which of the following measures reflects the equity dimension of the Draft STIP 2020?
o: Inclusion of women, marginalised groups and LGBTQ+ persons, along with day-care facilities at funded laboratories
Exclusion of marginalised communities from research governance
Restriction of funded laboratories to male researchers
Removal of social support from scientific institutions
accepted.x: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed inclusion of women, marginalised groups and LGBTQ+ persons and also envisaged day-care facilities at funded laboratories.
accepted.tq: Recognise the option that combines the policy’s stated inclusion and support measures.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s:
Which of the following was associated with the Draft STIP 2020’s proposed international and knowledge-engagement measures?
1. Diaspora portal
2. Diplomacy for S&T
3. Traditional Knowledge Systems and grassroots innovators
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: The Draft STIP 2020 included a diaspora portal, Diplomacy for S&T, and support for Traditional Knowledge Systems and grassroots innovators.
accepted.tq: Check all listed institutional and outreach measures before selecting the complete code.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s:
The Draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling which of the following every five years?
1. Full-time equivalent researchers
2. Gross expenditure on research and development
3. Private share of gross expenditure on research and development
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The draft policy proposed doubling FTE researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years.
accepted.tq: Track the repeated quantitative target and avoid omitting the private-sector component.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT an outcome of the Draft STIP 2020?
accepted.x: Atal Innovation Mission was not an outcome of STIP 2020; it was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016 as a separate initiative promoting innovation among students. ONOS and RIEF were associated with the draft policy proposals.
accepted.tq: Use the separate-initiative trap: identify the programme established outside the policy.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Atal Innovation Mission was set up by NITI Aayog in:
accepted.x: Atal Innovation Mission was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016 and was a separate initiative from the Draft STIP 2020.
accepted.tq: Separate the establishment year of a related initiative from the year of the policy under examination.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: One Nation, One Subscription was approved by the Union Cabinet in November 2024 with an approximate allocation of:
accepted.x: One Nation, One Subscription was approved in November 2024 with an allocation of about ₹6,000 crore for the period 2025–27.
accepted.tq: Check the figure, time period and approval year together; distractors alter one of these details.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with the STI Policy, 2013?
o: Risky Idea Fund — support for high-risk innovation
Fund for Innovations for Social Inclusion — socially inclusive innovation
One Nation, One Subscription — STI Policy, 2013
Small idea–small money — support for small innovative ideas
accepted.x: One Nation, One Subscription is associated with the Draft STIP 2020 and was approved in 2024, not with the STI Policy, 2013. The other three were associated with the 2013 policy.
accepted.tq: Catch the cross-policy substitution by matching each instrument to its correct policy period.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the STI Policy, 2013:
1. It proposed intervention in about ten high-impact sectors.
2. It sought to use modern science to advance traditional knowledge.
3. It assigned agricultural research and development policy to the STI Policy rather than ICAR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 2013 policy envisaged direct STI intervention in about ten high-impact sectors and the use of modern science for traditional knowledge. Agricultural R&D policy was left to ICAR, making statement 3 incorrect.
accepted.tq: Identify the reversed institutional responsibility in the third statement.
accepted.sec: Policy → year, Prime Minister, core focus (SPR 1958, TPS 1983, STP 2003, STI 2013)

accepted.s: Which of the following proposed measures of the Draft STIP 2020 would most directly support accountability in science and technology governance?
o: Permanent continuation of every funded programme
accepted.x: Periodic review and exit strategies were proposed to improve accountability and enable the discontinuation or restructuring of programmes when necessary.
accepted.tq: Apply the governance principle to select the measure that creates review and corrective mechanisms.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes

accepted.s: The proposed Open Science Framework under the Draft STIP 2020 aimed at making publicly funded data available under which terms?
accepted.x: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed that publicly funded data should be made available under FAIR terms.
accepted.tq: Test the exact technical acronym instead of a similar-looking expansion.
accepted.sec: Draft STIP 2020 - proposals and outcomes
